imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: The Red Room. Cast/design continuity: Two fictional brothers: younger with tousled brown hair and ochre sweater, older with dark cropped hair and faded blue shirt. Childhood in an immaculate cream-white living room with one red drink; decades later the same recognizably distinct men, lightly aged, at a family reunion. Grandmother has silver hair and a grey dress. Red remains one restrained visual echo.. CELL 0: Wide immaculate white living room. Two young brothers perch naturally on a low cream sofa; the younger glances nervously toward the doorway while holding a small glass of red drink near a side table. The older leans forward with a cautious steadying hand. Feet and furniture align credibly. CELL 1: Same room and boys. The red drink tips from the small glass onto pale upholstery as the older brother reaches too late to steady it. One modest spreading red stain is the dramatic event; keep hands attached, gravity readable, no giant splash or slapstick collision. CELL 2: Grandmother stands in the doorway, stern but human. Younger brother points uncertainly toward older brother, who freezes and looks back with hurt surprise. The spilled glass and red stain remain in view. No punishment, strike or invented reaction beyond the question and blame. CELL 3: Decades later, both brothers visibly adult and individually recognizable at a modest family reunion table. Warm conversation occurs around them while the older brother sits still with a withheld smile. Younger brother notices his face. A small red napkin quietly echoes the old stain, not a magical flashback. CELL 4: Outside the reunion in a quiet garden path, the younger adult brother faces the older at a respectful distance. His hands are open and low, posture undefended as he accepts blame. The older listens, eyes fixed on him. No family audience or forced embrace. CELL 5: Same two adult brothers on the garden path. The older brother’s eyes soften slightly as he answers; younger stands still, allowing the answer to land. Their bodies face one another naturally with a small respectful space between them. One red leaf near the path is the only remaining color echo. Editorial limit: Show two distinct brothers across age, not one person doubled. No invented punishment or instant absolution.
